ledger.note: 1557: 'he defeated Akizuki Kiyotane and seized Chikuzen Province.'

1558: 'Mōri captured Moji castle from the Ōuchi'; in September 1559 Sōrin recaptured it but the Mōri 'quickly took the castle again'. The Ōuchi's Yoshinaga (Sōrin's younger brother) had been forced to suicide by Mōri Motonari in 1557.
1569: Tatarahama. Sōrin 'attacked them at Tatarahama, forcing the Mōri to retreat and allowing him to retake Tachibana castle'; he 'threatened the Mōri foothold in Buzen Province'.
By 1569: 'Sōrin controlled Bungo, most of Buzen, Chikuzen, and Chikugo'. The page dates Chikugo only as of 'this time'; the holders are not named.

sources.title: Ōtomo clan
sources.note: Home province Bungo and Buzen, shugo from 1185; at its zenith under Sorin six provinces (Buzen, Bungo, Hizen, Higo, Chikuzen, Chikugo) and two half-provinces (Hyuga and Iyo); the clan retained domains into the Edo period.

sources.title: Ōtomo Sōrin
sources.note: Tenure 1550-1587; Funai Domain in Bungo inherited; 1557 seized Chikuzen from Akizuki Kiyotane; 1558 Mori captured Moji; Sept 1559 Sorin retook Moji, Mori retook it quickly; 1564 moved against the Ryuzoji of Hizen; by 1569 Bungo, most of Buzen, Chikuzen and Chikugo, influence over Higo, Hizen and Iyo (the Seven-Province Host); 1569 Tatarahama; 1578 Tsuchimochi in Hyuga, then Mimigawa lost; Hetsugigawa 1586; died June 1587.

sources.title: Battle of Mimigawa
sources.note: 10 December 1578 on the Mimi River in Hyuga; Shimazu victory; Otomo commanders killed.

sources.title: Shimazu Yoshihisa
sources.note: 1585 Horikiri in Chikugo and Iwaya in Chikuzen; mid-1585 the Shimazu controlled Chikugo, Chikuzen, Hizen, Higo, Hyuga, Osumi and Satsuma, Otomo the exception; 1586 marched on Otomo's Tachibana castle.

sources.title: Kyūshū campaign
sources.note: 1586 the Shimazu lifted the Tachibana siege and seized Funai Castle from the Otomo; Bungo fell to them after Hetsugigawa; the Otomo were supported by Sengoku Hidehisa, Sogo Masayasu and Chosokabe Motochika.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Ōtomo clan, Ōtomo Sōrin, Battle of Mimigawa, Shimazu Yoshihisa, Kyūshū campaign). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. Dated by the pages: Chikuzen (1557), Chikugo (by 1569), the losses (Hyūga half 1578, Chikuzen and Chikugo 1585, Bungo 1586). Page conflicts: the clan page counts six provinces and two half-provinces (Buzen, Bungo, Hizen, Higo, Chikuzen, Chikugo; Hyūga and Iyo) at the peak, the Sōrin page counts Bungo, most of Buzen, Chikuzen and Chikugo as held, with Higo, Hizen and Iyo under influence; this dossier follows the Sōrin page for the shape. The Yoshihisa page has Bungo as the Ōtomo's in mid-1585; the Kyūshū campaign page has Bungo fall to the Shimazu in 1586 (the Yoshihisa page is silent on that). The Sōrin page's request for Hideyoshi's aid is undated ('later' in 1585) and then the Hetsugigawa defeat in 1586. The Ōtomo clan page says the clan retained domains into the Edo period and gives no date for the loss of the domain in the 1590s (which is not on the pages). Not on the pages: Buzen as a map (Ōita Prefecture includes its northern part; Fukuoka's eastern strip is left out), Higo, Hizen and Iyo holdings. The Shimazu dossier carries the Chikuzen, Chikugo and Bungo gains and the Hyūga half (bridged); the Toyotomi dossier takes Bungo from the Shimazu in 1587. Counterpart strings: 'mori-clan' (no dossier yet) and 'shimazu-clan' (exists); others are clans named on the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
